The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build process for the `perl-struct-codec` package from CPAN. It retrieves the source tarball from `search.cpan.org`, which is the official Perl module repository, and verifies its integrity using both MD5 and SHA-512 checksums. The build process uses standard Perl module installation commands (`Makefile.PL`, `make`, `make install`) with appropriate environment variables to ensure installation into the package directory under vendor paths.

No suspicious operations are present: there are no network requests during build or package phases beyond the initial source download, no use of `eval`, `base64`, or obfuscated code, and no attempts to exfiltrate data or modify system files outside the package directory. The `check()` function appropriately runs tests in a controlled environment. All actions are consistent with standard Perl module packaging practices on Arch Linux.

The use of `search.cpan.org` (which redirects to `metacpan.org`) is normal for older CPAN packages, and while the HTTP URL is not HTTPS, this is not uncommon in CPAN-based PKGBUILDs and does not constitute a supply-chain attack vector when combined with verified checksums. The checksums are provided and non-skipped, adding verification integrity.
</details>
